courses.title: CPR for Healthcare Providers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation that meets current Emergency Cardiac Care (ECC) guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation education for Healthcare Providers. Equivalent to HLT 105 .

courses.title: Emergency Medical Technician
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisite: EMS 100 /equivalent. Co-requisite: EMS 120 .
courses.description: Prepares student for certification as a Virginia and National Registry EMT. Focuses on all aspects of pre-hospital basic life support as defined by the Virginia Office of Emergency Medical Services curriculum for Emergency Medicine Technician.

courses.title: Emergency Medical Technician-Basic I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares student for certification as a Virginia and/or National Registry EMT-Basic. Focuses on all aspects of pre-hospital basic life support as defined by the Virginia office of Emergency Medical Services curriculum for Emergency Medicine Technician Basic.

courses.title: Emergency Medical Technician-Basic II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues preparation of student for certification as a Virginia and/or National Registry EMT-Basic. Includes all aspects of pre-hospital basic life support as defined by the Virginia Office of Emergency Medical Services curriculum for Emergency Medicine Technician Basic.

courses.title: Emergency Medical Technician - Clinical
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. This course is a co-requisite for either EMS 111 or EMS 113 , depending upon the program in which the student is participating.
courses.description: Provides supervised direct patient contact introducing the student to the assessment and emergency care of sick and injured patients.

courses.title: Preparatory Foundations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts established by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Advanced EMT and Paramedic curricula. Includes EMS systems, introduction to research, workforce safety and wellness, EMS system communications, introduction to public health, legal and ethical issues.

courses.title: EMS Clinical Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS.
courses.description: Introduces the student to local clinical agencies and prepares the student for clinical activities above the level of EMT. Includes prerequisites required by clinical affiliates, therapeutic communication, primary assessment, history taking, secondary assessment, reassessment, monitoring devices and documentation.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 126 .
courses.description: Prepares students to demonstrate competency concerning basic principles of pharmacology, drug dosage calculations and medication administration. Introduces medications listed in the Advanced EMT (AEMT) scope of practice.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacology Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 125 .
courses.description: Focuses on the safe administration of medications in the emergency setting. Includes drug dose calculation and covers multiple routes of administration including oral, intramuscular, subcutaneous, intravenous, and intraosseous and other methods within the scope of practice for the emergency care provider.

courses.title: Airway, Shock and Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 128 .
courses.description: Introduces concepts associated with pre-hospital emergency care of the individual experiencing airway difficulty or in need of resuscitation or shock management.

courses.title: Airway, Shock and Resuscitation Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 127 .
courses.description: Focuses on specific skills related to airway, resuscitation and shock management.

courses.title: Emergency Medical Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 136 .
courses.description: Prepares the student to assess and manage patients with common medical emergencies.

courses.title: Emergency Medical Care Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 135 .
courses.description: Focuses on specific skills related to the assessment and management of common medical emergencies.

courses.title: Trauma Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Corequisite: EMS 138
courses.description: Prepares the student to assess and manage injured patients, developing his/her problem-solving ability in the treatment of trauma involving various body systems.

courses.title: Trauma Care Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 137 .
courses.description: Focuses on the skills required for the assessment and management of patients with traumatic injury.

courses.title: Special Populations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 140 .
courses.description: Focuses on the pre-hospital assessment and management of patients in a specific population including pediatrics, geriatrics, obstetrics/gynecology (OB/GYN), bariatric, abuse, sexual assault and special needs.

courses.title: Special Populations Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hour. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 139 .
courses.description: Develops skills related to the assessment and management of patients in a specific population including pediatrics, geriatrics, obstetrics/gynecology (OB/GYN), bariatric, abuse, sexual assault and special needs.

courses.title: Cardiovascular Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 142 .
courses.description: Focuses on assessment and management of cardiac-related emergencies. Covers basic dysrhythmia recognition and relates it to overall cardiac patient care.

courses.title: Cardiovascular Care Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite EMS 141 .
courses.description: Focuses on skills involved in the assessment and management of cardiac-related emergencies. Develops competency in basic dysrhythmia recognition and overall cardiac patient care.

courses.title: Advanced Emergency Medical Technician (AEMT)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS
courses.description: Prepares students to build upon content in the Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) curriculum and demonstrate competency in specific advanced skills and knowledge.

courses.title: Advanced EMT Completion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current EMT Certification and EMS 151 . Co-requisite: EMS 151 .
courses.description: Continues the Virginia Office of Emergency Medical Services Advanced, Intermediate and/or Paramedic curricula. Includes patient assessment, differential diagnosis and management of multiple complaints. Includes, but are not limited to conditions relating to diabetic, neurological, abdominal pain, environmental, behavioral, gynecology, and toxicological disease conditions. Also includes Advanced EMT level cardiac, trauma and special population topics.

courses.title: Prehospital Trauma Life Support (PHTLS)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisites: EMS 111 or equivalent.
courses.description: Prepares for certification as a Prehospital Trauma Life Support provider as defined by the American College of Surgeons.

courses.title: Advanced Medical Life Support (AMLS)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Covers current topics of care for adult patients suffering extensive medical conditions and emergencies, and offers certification as an Advanced Medical Life Support (AMLS) as defined by the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT).

courses.title: Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: EMS 100 or equivalent
courses.description: Prepares for certification as an Advanced Cardiac Life provider. Follows course as defined by the American Heart Association.

courses.title: Emergency Pediatric Care (EPC)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides a unique approach to pediatric medical care, offering assessment techniques that can help EMS practitioners rapidly and accurately assess pediatric patients to determine which situations may be life threatening and require immediate intervention. Offers certification as defined by the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT).

courses.title: Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Prepares the student for certification as a pediatric advanced life support provider as defined by the American Heart Association. Covers primary assessment and emergency care of infants and children.

courses.title: ALS Internship I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Begins the first in a series of clinical experiences providing supervised direct patient contact in appropriate patient care facilities in and out of hospitals. Includes but not limited to patient care units such as the Emergency Department, Critical Care units, Pediatric, Labor and Delivery, Operating Room, Trauma centers and various advanced life support units.

courses.title: Paramedic Clinical Experience I
courses.contact_hours: Internship 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS
courses.description: Introduces students to live patient assessment and management in the clinical setting. Begins a continuum of learning involving live patients that leads to entry-level competence at the paramedic level.

courses.title: Advanced EMS Foundations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts established by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for the Advanced EMT curriculum. Includes EMS systems, introduction to research, workforce safety and wellness, EMS system communications, therapeutic communication, and legal and ethical issues.

courses.title: Advanced Airway and Shock Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Co-requisite: EMS 182 : Advanced Airway & Shock Management Laboratory
courses.description: Introduces core principles of airway, shock, and resuscitation as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum. Provides students with a fundamental knowledge of the Cardiopulmonary system, including its assessment and management of shock. Covers cardiac arrest and post-arrest management.

courses.title: Advanced Airway and Shock Management Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Co-requisite: EMS 181 : Advanced Airway and Shock Management
courses.description: Examines assessment and management of trauma emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum. Provides students with specific skills related to airway, resuscitation and shock management.

courses.title: Advanced Medical Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 184 : Advanced Medical Care Laboratory
courses.description: Examines the assessment and management of medical emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum.

courses.title: Advanced Medical Care Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS program. Corequisite: EMS 183 : Advanced Medical Care
courses.description: Focuses on specific skills related to the assessment and management of common medical emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum.

courses.title: Advanced Trauma Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Co-requisite: EMS 186 : Advanced Trauma Care Laboratory
courses.description: Examines the assessment and management of trauma emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum.

courses.title: Advanced Trauma Care Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 185 : Advanced Trauma Care Laboratory
courses.description: Focuses on specific skills related to the assessment and management of trauma emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) within the Advanced EMT curriculum.

courses.title: Paramedic Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced pharmacological interventions, medications and their effects.

courses.title: Advanced Patient Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 204 .
courses.description: Focuses on the comprehensive assessment and management of patients in out-of-hospital and inter-facility scenarios. Content is centered on problem-solving through integration of didactic, psychomotor and affective curricula.

courses.title: Advanced Patient Care Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Corequisite: EMS 203
courses.description: Focuses on the comprehensive assessment and management of out-of-hospital and inter-facility patients using scenario-based learning.

courses.title: Pathophysiology for the Health Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the pathological processes of disease with emphasis on the anatomical and physiological alterations of the human body systems. Includes diagnosis and management appropriate to the advanced health care provider in and out of the hospital environment.

courses.title: EMS Operations
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on matters related to Emergency Medical Services (EMS) operations, incident and scene safety and awareness, triage, multiple and mass casualty incident operations and medical incident management (command and control of EMS incidents).

courses.title: Leadership and Professional Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the development of leadership within the field of Emergency Medical Services (EMS), topics include civic engagement, personal wellness, resource management, ethical considerations in leadership and research.

courses.title: Paramedic Review
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the student with intensive review for the practical and written portions of the National Registry Paramedic exam. May be repeated once, for credit.

courses.title: Paramedic Cardiovascular Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 222 : Paramedic Cardiovascular Care Laboratory
courses.description: Covers in-depth assessment and management of cardiovascular conditions, as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics.

courses.title: Paramedic Cardiovascular Care Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 221 : Paramedic Cardiovascular Care
courses.description: Focuses on skills involved in the assessment and management of cardiac-related emergencies as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics. Develops competency in basic dysrhythmia recognition and overall cardiac patient care.

courses.title: Paramedic Patient Care I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 224 : Paramedic Patient Care I Laboratory
courses.description: Covers the breadth of medical and trauma conditions as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics. Part I of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Patient Care I Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 223 : Paramedic Patient Care I
courses.description: Covers the skills related to the breadth of medical and trauma conditions as outlined by the NationalEmergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics. Part I of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Patient Care II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 226 : Paramedic Patient Care II Lab
courses.description: Covers the depth of medical and trauma conditions as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics. Part II of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Patient Care Laboratory II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS. Corequisite: EMS 225 : Paramedic Patient Care II.
courses.description: Covers the skills related to the depth of medical and trauma conditions as outlined by the National Emergency Medical Service Education Standards (NEMSES) for Paramedics. Part II of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Internship I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS.
courses.description: Introduces students to live patient assessment and management in the clinical and field setting. Begins a continuum of learning involving live patients that leads to entry-level competence at the paramedic level. Part I of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Internship II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: Current Virginia EMT and CPR certification as approved by the Virginia Office of EMS.
courses.description: Introduces students to live patient assessment and management in the clinical and field set. Continues the learning experience with live patients that leads to entry-level competence at the paramedic level. Part II of II.

courses.title: Paramedic Clinical Experience II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the student experience with live patient assessment and management in the clinical setting. It is the second step in a continuum of learning involving live patients that leads to entry-level competence at the paramedic level.

courses.title: Paramedic Comprehensive Field Experience
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Expands the student experience with live patient assessment and management into the field setting. It is the third step in a continuum of learning involving live patients that leads to entry-level competence at the paramedic level.

courses.title: Paramedic Capstone Internship
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 6 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides summative evaluation of the Paramedic student in the cognitive, psychomotor, and affective domains.

courses.title: ALS Refresher
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews material covered in the ALS programs. Meets all required criteria for recertification eligibility.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Energy Industry Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a broad understanding of the electric and natural gas utility industry and the energy generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure. Covers business models, regulations, types of energy and their conversion to useable energy such as electric power, how generated power is transmitted and distributed to the point of use, emerging technologies, and the connection to careers in the energy industry.

courses.title: Basic Occupational Communication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops ability to communicate in occupational situations. Involves writing, reading, speaking, and listening. Builds practical skills such as handling customer complaints, writing various types of letters, and preparing for a job interview. (Intended for certificate and diploma students.)

courses.title: Practical Writing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops writing ability for study, work, and other areas of life with emphasis on occupational correspondence and reports. Guides students in learning writing as a process: understanding audience and purpose, exploring ideas and information, composing, revising, and editing. Supports writing by integrating experiences in thinking, reading, listening, and speaking. Part I of II.

courses.title: Critical Reading and Study Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Helps students improve their reading and learning processes. Includes advanced comprehension strategies and study skills such as time management, note-taking, studying from textbooks and other reading materials, taking examinations, and using the library.

courses.title: College Composition I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces and prepares students to the critical processes and fundamentals of writing in academic and professional contexts. Teaches the use of print and digital technologies to promote inquiry. Requires the production of a variety of academic texts, totaling at least 4500 words (15 pages typed) of polished writing. This course requires proficiency in using word processing and learning management software. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: College Composition II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111
courses.description: Further develops students' ability to write for academic and professional contexts with increased emphasis on argumentation and research. Requires students to evaluate, integrate, and document print and digital sources to produce a range of academic and multimodal texts, culminating in a fully documented research paper. This course requires proficiency in using word processing and learning management software. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Technical-Professional Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111
courses.description: Develops ability in technical writing through extensive practice in composing technical reports and technical documents. Guides students in achieving voice, tone, style, and content in formatting, editing, and graphics. Introduces students to technical discourse through selected readings. Provides instruction and practice in basic principles of oral communication/presentation. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Technical Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops ability in technical writing through extensive practice in composing technical reports and other documents. Guides students in achieving voice, tone, style, and content in formatting, editing, and graphics. Introduces students to technical discourse through selected reading. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ENG 113 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Writing for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops ability in business writing through extensive practice in composing business correspondence and other documents. Guides students in achieving voice, tone, style, and content appropriate to a specific audience and purpose. Includes instruction in formatting and editing. Introduces students to business discourse through selected readings.

courses.title: Introduction to Journalism
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 department approval.
courses.description: Introduces students to the practice of journalism through researching, interviewing, writing, editing and revising articles for potential publication. Explores current issues in the field, media law, journalistic values, ethics and reporting. Acquaints students with Associated Press Style, copy editing, news and feature writing, and creative journalism.

courses.title: Introduction to Journalism II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 OR 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces students to all news media, especially news gathering and preparation for print. Part II of II.

courses.title: Writing for the World Wide Web
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or approval.
courses.description: Teaches students how to outline, compose, organize, and edit written materials for publication on the World Wide Web. Teaches students how to design basic web pages, compose website content, design web site layout and develop website navigation for a variety of possible audiences.

courses.title: Introduction to Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 .
courses.description: Introduces students to a range of literary genres that may include poetry, fiction, drama, creative nonfiction, and other cultural texts, as it continues to develop college writing.

courses.title: Technical Report Writing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers a review of organizational skills including paragraph writing and basic forms of technical communications, various forms of business correspondence, and basic procedures for research writing. Includes instruction and practice in oral communication skills. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ENG 113 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111
courses.description: Introduces the scientific study of language. Focuses on brain and language, phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics and pragmatics, and first and second language acquisition.

courses.title: Advanced Composition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Helps students refine skills in writing non-fiction prose. Guides development of individual voice and style. Introduces procedures for publication.

courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Explores fundamentals of writing imaginatively in genres such as poetry, fiction, drama, and essays. Examines terminology and techniques through readings about the craft of creative writing and model texts and provides students the opportunity to apply these techniques in their own writing. Requires students to develop and revise original work through peer and instructor feedback.

courses.title: Creative Writing II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces the student to the fundamentals of writing imaginatively. Students write in forms to be selected from poetry, fiction, drama, and essays. Part II of II.

courses.title: Creative Writing - Poetry I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamentals and techniques of writing poetry. Part I of II.

courses.title: Reading Literature: Culture and Ideas
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval.
courses.description: Examines a set of literary texts linked by a particular theme, with inquiry into the historical, cultural, and/or social contexts of the texts and the theme. Emphasizes interpretive and critical analysis skills developed through close reading and intertextual study, as well as highlights an exploration of cultural ideas. Engages works of diverse genres, authors, and time periods. Specific themes will vary by section. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Mystery in Literature and Film
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies the mystery as a genre, including history, types and cultural aspects of stories, novels, plays, film adaptions. Involves critical reading, writing, and viewing.

courses.title: Introduction to the Short Story
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Examines the complexity of the human experience through short stories across a diverse range of cultures and traditions. Develops skills in close reading, writing, research, interpretation, and comparative analysis.

courses.title: Survey of American Literature I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Examines American literary works from colonial times to the present, emphasizing the ideas and characteristics of our national literature. Involves critical reading and writing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Survey of American Literature II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Examines American literary works from colonial times to the present, emphasizing the ideas and characteristics of our national literature. Involves critical reading and writing.Part II of II.

courses.title: Survey of English Literature I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies major English works from the Anglo-Saxon period to the present, emphasizing ideas and characteristics of the British literary tradition. Involves critical reading and writing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Survey of English Literature II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies major English works from the Anglo-Saxon period to the present, emphasizing ideas and characteristics of the British literary tradition. Involves critical reading and writing. Part II of II.

courses.title: British Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval,
courses.description: Examines British literary traditions and texts from diverse time periods, genres, and authors. Develops critical thinking and interpretive skills through close reading, discussion, and analysis of literary texts in their historical, cultural, social, and/or literary contexts. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: American Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval.
courses.description: Examines American literary traditions and texts from diverse time periods, genres, and authors. Analyzes literary works within their historical, cultural, social, and/or literary contexts. Emphasizes skills of close reading. Develops critical thinking and interpretive skills through discussion, interpretation, and analysis of these texts. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Survey of Popular Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Analyzes familiar aspects of American culture, as seen through popular literature, with additional emphasis on television, film, and popular art.

courses.title: Children's Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval.
courses.description: Examines the history and development of children's literature of diverse genres, time periods, and authors. Focuses on analysis of texts for literary qualities and audience. Develops critical thinking and interpretive skills through close reading, discussion, and analysis of literary texts. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval.
courses.description: Examines literary texts across a variety of cultures, genres, and time periods. Develops critical thinking and interpretive skills through close reading, discussion, and analysis of literary texts from around the world in their historical, cultural, social, and/or literary contexts. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Mythological Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies a variety of mythological works of literature, along with an examination of the allegorical and metaphorical themes within each work, and an understanding of figurative language, symbology and mythical allusions.

courses.title: African American Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval.
courses.description: Explores the stories African American authors tell about themselves, their communities, and the world. Examines common and diverging themes within African American literary traditions through the study of diverse authors, genres, and literary movements from a variety of time periods. Emphasizes interpretive and critical analysis skills developed through close reading and consideration of historical and cultural contexts. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: The Works of Shakespeare I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Examines selected works of Shakespeare. Involves critical reading and writing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Women in Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 , ENG 113 , or departmental approval
courses.description: Examines literary texts by women writers from diverse time periods, genres, and authors. Develops skills of close reading and literary analysis through analysis of texts within their historical, cultural, social, and/or literary contexts. Explores how women's experiences have shaped their literary contributions, the cultural forces affecting their lives, and how they have used writing to shape their cultures. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Film and Literature
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 112 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Examines the translation of literature into film viewing and writing.

courses.title: Foundations of Environmental Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic physical, chemical, and biological principles with an emphasis on the interactions between humans and the environment. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written and oral communication, and basic mathematical skills. Intended for students not majoring in science. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course. Can be taken by itself or before or after ENV 122 .

courses.title: Applications in Environmental Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies the basic concepts of environmental science to human interactions with the environment. Examines environmental science in the context of the societal implications with a focus on sustainability. Assignments require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, and basic mathematical skills. Intended for students not majoring in science. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Environmental Principles in Public Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines critical factors involved in environmental/public health administration in the current post-911 society. Includes basic risk analysis and fate and transport modeling, environmental microbiology and toxicology with implications on genetics, GIS, bioterrorism, and infectious diseases.

courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Environmental Problems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the relationship of man to his environment; ecological principles, population dynamics, topics of current importance including air, water, and noise pollution; poisoning and toxicity, radiation, conservation and management of natural resources.

courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces environmental law including the history of environmental laws, the National Environment Policy Act, state environmental acts, hazardous wastes, endangered species, pollution, and surface mine reclamation.

courses.title: GIS: Applications in Environmental Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: GIS 200 .
courses.description: Introduces Global Positioning Systems(GPS) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) hardware and software and applies the principles of GPS and GIS to Forest Science and Environmental Science. Includes: Natural Disasters; Pest Control; Water Quality; Prescribed Burning; Identifying Sources of Pollution.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Oral and Written Communications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practice in the sound, stress, intonation, structural patterns, grammar, vocabulary, and idioms of beginning-level English. Prerequisite: Requires ability to understand short spoken passages as well as familiarity with basic grammatical structure.

courses.title: Programming Methods for Electrical/Electronic Calcula.
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the application of a high-level language to electrical and electronic problem solving and circuit analysis. Introduces an operating system.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Fundamentals I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies D.C. and A.C. circuits, basic electrical components, instruments, network theorems, and techniques used to predict, analyze and measure electrical quantities. Part I of II.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Fundamentals II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies D.C. and A.C. circuits, basic electrical components, instruments, network theorems, and techniques used to predict, analyze and measure electrical quantities. Part II of II.

courses.title: D.C. and A.C. Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies current flow in direct and alternating current circuits with emphasis upon practical problems. Reviews mathematics used in circuit calculations. Introduces concepts of resistance, capacitance, inductance and magnetism. Focuses on electronics/circuits application.

courses.title: Electronic Applications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 2-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides laboratory and shop experience as applied to basic electronic devices, circuits and systems with emphasis on practical measurements. Part I of II.

courses.title: Amplifiers and Integrated Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies devices and amplifiers with emphasis on analysis and design. May include summing and integrating amplifiers, choppers, modulators and other circuits.

courses.title: PC Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 3-7 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the maintenance, troubleshooting and repair of personal computer systems. Uses IBM or compatible computer systems to provide fault isolation drill and practice.

courses.title: Machine Control Using Relay & Programmable Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to hardwired relay logic and the programmable logic controller (PLC) as utilized in a variety of different control tasks. Covers different types of inputs and outputs in control system. Teaches practical troubleshooting strategies.

courses.title: Survey of Microprocessors
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of microprocessor architecture, basic machine language programming, and I/O devices.

courses.title: Logic Circuits and Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies digital switching and logic circuits, numbering systems, Boolean algebra, logic gates and families. Includes fundamental concepts of microprocessor operation and interface circuitry.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Cooperative Education

courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Electronic Devices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory.
courses.description: Studies active devices and circuits such as diodes, power supplies, transistors, amplifiers and others. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Devices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory.
courses.description: Studies active devices and circuits such as diodes, power supplies, transistors, amplifiers and others. Part II of II.

courses.title: Electronic Controls I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses characteristics and performance of linear control systems with one or more feedback loops. Includes functions and properties of various components encountered in control systems including servo-amplifiers and error detectors, machine synchronization for automatic operations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Communications I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies noise, information and bandwidth, modulation and demodulation, transmitters and receivers, wave propagation, antennas and transmission lines. Includes broad band communication systems, microwave, both terrestrial and satellite, fiber optics, multiplexing and associated hardware. Part I of II.

courses.title: Electronic Communications II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies noise, information and bandwidth, modulation and demodulation, transmitters and receivers, wave propagation, antennas and transmission lines. Includes broad band communication systems, microwave, both terrestrial and satellite, fiber optics, multiplexing and associated hardware. Part II of II.

courses.title: Solid State Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Knowledge of D.C./A.C. theory, and active devices and circuits.
courses.description: Teaches theory and application of amplifiers and oscillators. Includes amplifier circuit configurations, amplifier classes, operational amplifiers, power amplifiers, bandwidth distortion, and principles of feedback.

courses.title: Microprocessor Application I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the fundamentals of microprocessors including architecture, internal operations, memory, I/O devices machine level programming and interfacing. Emphasizes instrumentation and microprocessor. Part I of II.

courses.title: Microprocessor Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of microprocessors including architecture, internal operations, memory, I/O devices, machine level programming and interfacing.

courses.title: Computer Electronics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of digital electronics and microprocessors to familiarize the student with typical circuits and methods used to interface computer and/or controllers with various I/O devices. Includes exposure to high level programming as well as assembly language routines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Computer Electronics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of digital electronics and microprocessors to familiarize the student with typical circuits and methods used to interface computer and/or controllers with various I/O devices. Includes exposure to high level programming as well as assembly language routines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Computer Interfacing and Circuitry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Deals with typical circuitry used to interface computers with the outside world.

courses.title: Digital Principles, Terminology and Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies digital principles, terminology and applications covering number systems, arithmetic, Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps and advanced logic circuits. Includes the study of registers, encoding and decoding, and multiplexing; A/D, D/A, displays and others.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Logic Circuits and Computers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies digital logic, Boolean algebra, and arithmetic circuits, using standard integrated circuits and the functional block approach. Introduces concepts of computers, the internal operation and control language.

courses.title: Digital Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes basic numbering systems, Boolean algebra, logic circuits and systems, pulse circuits and pulse logic systems as applied to computer and microprocessor technology.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Microcomputer Repair
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the student with an exposure to the various techniques and procedures used to troubleshoot a microcomputer. courses.title: Conversation in French II

courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Part I of II.

courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Part II of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Conversation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: FRE 211 or assessment of instructor.
courses.description: Continues to develop fluency through emphasis on idioms and other complex sentence structures. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the global patterns and processes of the atmosphere, biosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere. Explores Earth?s physical systems and the interrelationships among them through studying Earth-Sun geometry, climate and weather phenomena, landforms, biomes, and environmental change.

courses.title: People and the Land: Intro to Cultural Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to themes in human geography and the ways in which human geographers study spatial relationships in the world. Emphasizes geospatial tools and concepts to examine global patterns of human demographics, culture, geopolitics, and economic and environmental interdependence through introduction to a broad range of subject matter. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Regional Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines similarities and differences among the world's major regions. Evaluates ways in which people and places interact across space and time to produce particular spatial and environmental patterns. Introduces the student to geographic tools such as maps. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Economic Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the subfield of human geography by focusing on the key interactions of people, space, and economics. Familiarizes students with economic, geographic, political and demographic factors that impact international target markets and trade activity. Focuses on levels of development, urban areas, globalization, and international trade

courses.title: Political Geography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the influence of geography on political systems and nation states. Discusses historic and current events including campaigns, wars, trade, and treaties as functions of land, resources and energy requirements. Introduces students to types and uses of maps

Teaches the introductory concepts of geographic location and problem solving by using GIS and GPS units in demonstrating solutions to cross-curricular applications of the technology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Geographical Information Systems II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: GIS 200 .

courses.title: Physical Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the science of physical geology through a comprehensive systems-based examination of Earth's structure, composition, rocks and minerals, landforms, geomorphology, and agents responsible for shaping and modifying its environments. Explores the origin and evolution of Earth's topographic and bathymetric features, geologic phenomena, and geologic hazards, resulting from plate tectonics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Historical Geology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Traces the evolution of the earth and life through time. Presents scientific theories of the origin of the earth and life and interprets rock and fossil record. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Earth Systems: An Environmental Geology Perspective
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts in earth systems including earth materials, plate tectonics, weathering, surface and groundwater, wasting, volcanoes, earthquakes and coastal, as well as pollution and climate change. Explores major topics relating human interaction with the physical environment through case studies. Reinforces applications through laboratory experiments, demonstrations, and field studies. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Oceanography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part I of II.

courses.title: Oceanography II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the dynamics of the oceans and ocean basins. Applies the principles of physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography. Part II of II.

Utilizes current coding standards in identifying payment methodologies, revenue cycle management and reimbursement.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Pre-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from ancient times to 1600 CE. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Post-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from 1600 CE to the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Pre-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Europe from antiquity to approximately 1500. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Post-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas from approximately 1500 CE through the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from its origins to 1877. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History Since 1865
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from 1865 to present. Includes major political, social and economic developments since 1865, overseas expansion, the two world wars, the Cold War and the post-Cold War era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of the American Indian

courses.title: History of Russia I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys history of Russia from earliest times to the present. Includes political, economic, multi-national, social, and cultural aspects of Russian and Soviet history. Part I of II.

courses.title: History of the Ancient World I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the history of the ancient world from the dawn of civilization in the Near East to the fall of Rome. Part I of II.

courses.title: Topics in Cultural Ethnicity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Cultural experiences of various ethnic groups in the United States, e.g. the Irish, Italians, Jews, Germans, etc.

courses.title: United States History in Film
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected topics in the United States history which shaped the American experience, presented in film.

courses.title: Military History of the Civil War
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes military campaigns of the Civil War, including factors contributing to the defeat of the Confederacy and problems created by the war. May include field trips to Civil War sites in the region.

courses.title: The Second World War
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines causes and consequences of the Second World War. Includes the rise of totalitarianism, American neutrality, military developments, the home fronts, diplomacy, and the decision to use the atomic bomb.

courses.title: The American Constitution
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes the origin and development of the United States Constitution. Includes the evolution of civil liberties, property rights, contracts, due process, judicial review, federal-state relationships, and corporate-government relations.

courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies factors that led to the division between the States. Examines the war, the home fronts, and the era of Reconstruction.

courses.title: United States History Since World War II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates United States history from 1945 to the present, studying both domestic developments and American involvement in international affairs.

courses.title: The American Experience in Vietnam
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes American involvement in Vietnam from World War II with emphasis on the presidencies of Johnson, Nixon and Ford.

courses.title: American Foreign Policy Since 1890
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines American foreign policy since 1890 with an emphasis on current events and diverse points of view.

courses.title: History of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the cultural, economic, political, and religious history of Virginia from pre-contact to the present. courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of pharmacy practice, drug classifications and generic substitutions, and the role and responsibility of a pharmacy technician professional. Focuses on the essentials required for excelling in the pharmacy technician role.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: First Aid and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety and first aid.

courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of health and dimensions of wellness through exploration of a variety of personal health topics. Identifies factors that affect the health status of individuals in addition to health promotion and disease prevention at the personal and community level.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces and focuses on the principles of personal and community health.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal Wellness Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the dimensions of wellness including the physical, emotional, environmental, spiritual, occupational, and social components.

courses.title: Substance Abuse: Prevention and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the use and abuse of drugs in contemporary society with emphasis upon sociological, physiological, and psychological effects of drugs.

courses.title: Nutrition and Diet Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrients, sources, functions, and requirements with an introduction to diet therapy. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Child Health and Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the physical needs of the preschool child and the methods by which these are met. Emphasizes health routines, hygiene, nutrition, feeding and clothing habits, childhood diseases, and safety as related to health growth and development.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies nutrient components of food, including carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals and water. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 230 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Orientation to Health Related Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1- 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the interrelated roles and functions of various members of the health team.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on medical terminology for students preparing for careers in the health professions. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Medical Terminology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems, and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation, and usage. Emphasizes more complex skills and techniques in understanding medical terminology. Part II of II. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. HLT 143 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of human sexuality. Includes anatomy, physiology, pregnancy, family planning, venereal diseases, and sexual variations.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of various forms of physical activity and how they promote human health. Examines the study of physical activity from the perspectives of professional practice, scholarly study and experience. Provides a broad overview of the history, scientific principles, methodologies, and research among the major subdisciplines to prepare students for further study in kinesiology and health sciences. Explores current issues, future directions, certifications, professional associations, and career opportunities.

courses.title: Personal Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of stress and explores its physical, psychological and social effects. Includes the relationships among stress and change, self-evaluation, sources of stress, and ways to develop current coping skills for handling stress. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: General Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes general pharmacology for the health related professions covering general principles of drug actions/reactions, major drug classes, specific agent within each class, and routine mathematical calculations needed to determine desired dosages.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part II of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy I Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience to supplement instruction in HLT 261 -262. Should be taken concurrently with HLT 261 -262, in appropriate curricula, as identified by the college. Part I of II.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II Lab
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience to supplement instruction in HLT 261 -262. Should be taken concurrently with HLT 261 -262, in appropriate curricula, as identified by the college. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills needed to function in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in attending, listening and responding. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per work.
courses.description: Expands the development of counseling skills needed to function effectively in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in responding, personalizing, summarizing and initiating. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement. Develops plans for achieving personal and program goals.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: The Helper As a Change Agent
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the following skills for implementing alternative models of change and influence: action research, problem- solving, consultation, workshop development, and outreach and advocacy for diverse client populations.

courses.title: Gerontology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the process of aging; its implications in relation to health, recreation, education, transportation, meaningful work or activity, and to community resources. Emphasizes experiencing the aging process, facilitating retirement, and application of the helping relationship to work with older adults.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides knowledge, skills, and insight for working in substance use programs. Emphasizes personal growth and client growth measures in helping relationships. Stresses various methods of individual and group techniques for helping the individual with substance use disorder.

courses.title: Substance Use Treatment II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HMS 251 .
courses.description: Expands knowledge and skill in working with individuals with substance use disorder. Focuses on assisting people with substance use disorder in individual and group settings and explores client treatment modalities. May provide opportunities for field experience in treatment centers.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hotel-Restaurant Organization and Management II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history, opportunities, problems and trends of the hospitality industry. Covers the organization of the various sectors of the hospitality industry including human resources, general business considerations, and management theory. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Sanitation and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the moral and legal responsibilities of management to insure a sanitary and safe environment in a food service operation. Emphasizes the causes and prevention of foodborne illnesses in conformity with federal, state and local guidelines. Focuses on OSHA standards in assuring safe working conditions.

courses.title: Stock, Soup, and Sauce Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of stocks, soups, and sauces. Promotes the knowledge/skills to prepare stocks, soups, and sauces, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Marketing of Hospitality Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and practices of marketing the services of the hotel and restaurant industry. Emphasizes the marketing concept with applications leading to customer satisfaction. Reviews methods of external and internal stimulation of sales. May include a practical sales/marketing exercise and computer applications.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: History of Garden Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the development of gardens as they chronicle the development of civilization. Introduces the periods, in both Europe and North America, beginning with settlement, on through industrial development, land and space utilization to current environmental concerns. Explores physical and cultural influences on garden design and utilization.

courses.title: Introduction to Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of basic table arrangements. Includes the history of design styles, identification of flowers and green, identification and use of equipment, and conditioning and handling of flowers.
